cleanIntro: The BANISH HNT 30 SS is a welded, tubeless stainless .30 hunting can, and BANISH says plainly that it is not designed to be fully disassembled — the six baffles do not come out. The only part you take off is the mount adapter in the HUB rear thread. Its whole service is a 24-hour soak, a brass brush down the blast chamber and a thorough clean of every thread, every 50 to 100 rounds. It is rated for centerfire cartridges of .30 calibre and smaller, up to .300 RUM. Everything about unloading your rifle comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Rifle unloaded, action open and visibly clear
steps.action: Before the can comes off, the rifle has to be unloaded with the action open so you can see it is empty. BANISH does not print a clearing procedure for your rifle. It sends you to that rifle's own manual, or to a licensed dealer, if you are not sure how.
steps.prose: A suppressed rifle is quieter, not safer. Treat it exactly as you would the same rifle without the can.
steps.quote: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.

steps.title: What it is rated for: centerfire, .30 calibre and smaller
steps.action: Check what the can has been fed. The HNT 30 SS is a centerfire can for .30 calibre and smaller, magnum-rated up to .300 RUM, and BANISH builds it for bolt-action rifles. Rimfire is not in its stated range.
steps.prose: If it has been on anything outside that range, stop here and talk to BANISH before you clean or fire it.
steps.aside: Compatible with centerfire cartridges up to .300 RUM
steps.quote: Ideally suited for bolt-action rifles, the magnumrated 30 SS is designed for use with centerfire cartridges, .30-caliber and smaller.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: The can stays hot long after the rifle stops feeling warm. Wait for it to cool, or use a suppressor cover or gloves, before you take hold of it to unscrew it.
steps.prose: Grabbing a hot can and twisting is how people get burned, and it is also when a joint that only needed hand pressure gets forced.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use a suppressor cover (sold separately) or gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Hot after firing. Cover or gloves.

steps.title: Unscrew the can off the barrel by hand
steps.action: With the rifle clear and the can cool, unscrew the suppressor off the barrel threads. It goes on hand tight only, so it should come off by hand. If it is stiff, that is fouling on the threads, not a torqued joint — forcing it is how barrel threads get damaged.
steps.prose: Direct-thread cans can work loose while firing. A can that has been loosening will often come off very easily.
steps.aside: Please note, the suppressor will be very hot during and after firing. Wait until the suppressor cools or use a suppressor cover (sold separately) to re-tighten.
steps.quote: Hand tighten suppressor only. Once snug, it is ready for use.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR (DIRECT THREAD), p.4

steps.title: Mount adapter out of the back — and that is as far as it opens
steps.action: Take the mount adapter out of the rear of the can. That is the ONLY part of the HNT 30 SS that comes off. The tube is welded and the baffles cannot be removed, so there is no end cap to unscrew and no baffle stack to pull. Anyone telling you to open it further is describing a different can.
steps.prose: The rear thread under the adapter is the HUB thread, which is why a different direct-thread or QD adapter can go in its place.
steps.quote: The welded-tubeless BANISH HNT 30 SS is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface can be removed for cleaning.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Thread protector on the muzzle while the can is off
steps.action: With the can off, fit a thread protector or another muzzle device to the barrel. Bare muzzle threads get dented in a case, and a dented thread is what cross-threads the can next time. It also protects the crown, which your accuracy depends on.
steps.prose: This is a storage and transport habit, not a cleaning step, and it costs nothing.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Twenty-four hour soak
steps.action: Put the whole can under cleaning solution, or seal the muzzle end and fill it, and leave it for 24 hours. Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or even dish soap all work. What does not is anything that strips the Cerakote.
steps.prose: The interval is every 50 to 100 rounds. Because the can never opens, the soak is the only thing that reaches the baffles, so do not cut it short.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50-100 rounds fired.
steps.quote: To clean, submerge the entire suppressor in cleaning solution. Or, seal the muzzle end of the suppressor and fill its interior with cleaning solution. In both cases, let the suppressor soak for 24 hours.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — CLEANING, p.6
steps.warn: Be sure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote finish.

steps.title: Brass brush the blast chamber
steps.action: After the soak, take a brass brush to the blast chamber at the rear of the can. That first chamber takes the hardest carbon, and it is the one part of the inside you can reach.
steps.prose: Brass, not steel. Brush the blast chamber only; nothing further inside is meant to be worked on.
steps.caution: The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.quote: Once soaked, use a brass brush to clean the blast chamber.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Threads — all of them, inside and out
steps.action: With the mount adapter out, clean every thread: the can's own rear threads, the adapter's inside and outside threads, and the barrel threads. Carbon left in a thread is what stops the can seating square against the barrel shoulder.
steps.prose: If your rifle has a muzzle brake with a crush washer under it, the washer must come out before the can goes on that barrel.
steps.quote: Remove the mounting adapter and thoroughly clean the threads, removing any debris or buildup. This includes the suppressor’s threads, as well as all internal and external mounting threads.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the rifle, the mount adapter is out, and everything has soaked, been brushed and had its threads cleaned. That is all BANISH publishes for the HNT 30 SS — the baffles stay where they are. Let it dry fully, put the adapter back in, and screw it back onto a clean barrel by hand.
steps.prose: There is no Deep Clean for this can, because BANISH publishes nothing beyond the mount adapter. At the next range session, fire 10 to 15 rounds through it to blow out what the soak loosened.
steps.quote: Once clean, allow the suppressor to dry. Re-install mounting adapters and reattach to firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH HNT 30 SS PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final"; its upload path is /2026/04/). — CLEANING, p.6

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the mount interface. BANISH publishes no procedure beyond taking out the mount adapter for the HNT 30 SS, and states why on its CLEANING page (p.6): 'The welded-tubeless BANISH HNT 30 SS is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface can be removed for cleaning.' The tube is welded, so there is nothing to take apart past the adapter, which the field strip already covers. Inventing a baffle-stack teardown would be borrowing a procedure from a different can.

cleaning.name: INTERIOR
tasks: Submerge the whole can, or seal the muzzle end and fill it, and soak 24 hours
Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or dish soap — nothing that strips Cerakote
Brass brush the blast chamber once it has soaked
Do NOT try to open the tube or remove the baffles — they are not removable

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Remove the mount adapter — the only removable part
Clean the can's own rear threads
Clean the adapter's inside AND outside threads
Clean the barrel threads; remove any crush washer under a muzzle brake before mounting

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: Let it dry fully before the adapter goes back in
Fire 10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session to blow out loosened debris
Fit a thread protector to the bare muzzle whenever the can is off

reassembly: Let the can dry completely, then put the mount adapter back into the rear thread.
Check that the barrel threads and the can's threads are clean and undamaged.
Line the threaded end of the can up with the barrel threads and start it by hand, taking care not to cross-thread it.
Screw it on until it seats firmly against the barrel shoulder — hand tight only, no tools.
Confirm there is no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor mount.
fncheck: Check the fit before you fire: on a direct-thread mount there must be NO visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor mount, and nothing may be blocking the can. If there is any gap, do not fire with the can on — a can not seated against the shoulder costs accuracy and can damage it. Once shooting, check it is still tight after the first 5 rounds and every 30 after that, letting it cool or using a cover before you re-tighten. At the next range session, fire 10-15 clearing rounds through it.
